outcome: A prevention effect stops the damage events it matches, so that damage is not dealt, and leaves other damage events alone.

note: the word prevent identifies prevention effects

outcome: A prevention effect lasts until it is used up or its duration ends, and prevents nothing after that.
A prevention effect created after the damage was dealt changes nothing; one created in response prevents it.
The additional effect of a prevention effect happens right after the prevention and uses the amount prevented.
Prevented damage is never dealt, so effects that need the damage dealt, such as deathtouch, do not happen.
A damage-amount shield prevents damage one point at a time across any number of events and lets the excess through once it reaches 0.
A next-time shield prevents the whole next instance of damage from the chosen source, and later instances are dealt normally.
A shield for a source with a property does not prevent damage once the source lacks the property, and is not used up.
A static prevent-N effect prevents N of each applicable damage event separately.
A radiance-style prevention gives a shield to each matching creature on the battlefield at resolution and not to creatures that enter later.
Unpreventable damage is dealt in full and does not reduce an existing prevention shield.

note: applying a prevention effect only once to unpreventable damage rules out a loop; no board difference shows it

outcome: An ability that triggers on prevented damage fires each time a prevention effect prevents some damage.
